proposals.before: She bore a son, Dezheng; at four [years] she became a widow.
proposals.after: She bore a son, Dezheng; when he was four she became a widow.
proposals.reason: Chinese 四歲而寡 dates the son's age at widowhood, not Lady Su's age.

proposals.before: Her mother-in-law, Lady He, went to fetch water from the brook and was gone a long time.
proposals.after: Her mother, Lady He, went to fetch water from the brook and was gone a long time.
proposals.reason: Chinese 母何氏 is mother, not 姑 (mother-in-law); the idiomatic rendering invents an in-law relation.

proposals.before: She suddenly heard a splash, rushed outside, and saw a tiger carrying her mother-in-law away in its mouth.
proposals.after: She suddenly heard a splash, rushed outside, and saw a tiger carrying her mother away in its mouth.
proposals.reason: Continues 母 from s0029; 其母 is her mother, not mother-in-law.

proposals.before: Yao carried her mother-in-law home, nursed her with medicine, and cared for her for more than twenty years until her death.
proposals.after: Yao carried her mother home, nursed her with medicine, and cared for her for more than twenty years until her death.
proposals.reason: Chinese 負母 is her mother; mother-in-law is unsupported.

proposals.before: Her husband's uncle was too ill to travel, so Zhang went back to prepare his medicine and meals and brought a sedan chair with her.
proposals.after: Her father-in-law was too ill to travel, so Zhang went back to prepare his medicine and meals and brought a sedan chair with her.
proposals.reason: In this wife-biography 舅 pairs with 姑 as father-in-law, not husband's uncle.

proposals.before: Her father-in-law's younger brother, because of illness, had not gone; Zhang returned to attend to medicines and food, and moreover had a sedan chair follow her of her own accord.
proposals.after: Her father-in-law, because of illness, had not gone; Zhang returned to attend to medicines and food, and moreover had a sedan chair follow her of her own accord.
proposals.reason: 舅 here is the father-in-law remaining at home while 夫與姑 guarded the stockade, not a younger brother of the father-in-law.

proposals.before: When bandits arrived, she ordered the sedan bearers to carry her uncle away while she herself faced the raiders.
proposals.after: When bandits arrived, she ordered the sedan bearers to carry her father-in-law away while she herself faced the raiders.
proposals.reason: 其舅 continues the father-in-law of s0050, not an uncle.

proposals.before: Before long bandits arrived; she immediately ordered that the sedan chair carry her uncle, while she herself encountered the bandits.
proposals.after: Before long bandits arrived; she immediately ordered that the sedan chair carry her father-in-law, while she herself encountered the bandits.
proposals.reason: 其舅 is the father-in-law already identified as 舅.

proposals.before: One soldier slashed her left arm, yet she yielded all the more stubbornly.
proposals.after: One soldier slashed her left arm, yet she was all the more unyielding.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'yielded all the more' contradicts 愈不屈 (became even less yielding); the literal field already has the correct sense.

proposals.before: The bandits rushed in and pulled her out.
proposals.after: The bandits rushed out and pulled her from the water.
proposals.reason: Chinese 賊競出之 describes the bandits going out to retrieve her, matching the literal field; 'rushed in' reverses the direction.

proposals.before: Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a scholar of Xuzhou.
proposals.after: Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a scholar of Xu Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu Prefecture near Xuchang, not Xuzhou (徐州).

proposals.before: Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a Confucian scholar of Xuzhou.
proposals.after: Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a Confucian scholar of Xu Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu Prefecture near Xuchang, not Xuzhou (徐州).

proposals.before: In Zhizheng 16 Zhang Shicheng besieged Hangzhou. His daughter Lin'annu cried out in alarm, "The rebels are here—Mother, forgive me, but I must find a way to die."
proposals.after: In Zhizheng 16 Zhang Shicheng besieged Hangzhou. Huang Zhongqi's daughter Lin'annu cried out in alarm, "The rebels are here—Mother, forgive me, but I must find a way to die."
proposals.reason: 其女臨安奴 is Huang Zhongqi and Lady Zhu's daughter, not Zhang Shicheng's; later units treat Zhu and Lin'annu as mother and daughter.

proposals.before: In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, Zhang Shicheng attacked Hangzhou; his daughter Lin'annu said in alarm, "The bandits are here—I take leave of my mother to seek death."
proposals.after: In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, Zhang Shicheng attacked Hangzhou; his (Huang Zhongqi's) daughter Lin'annu said in alarm, "The bandits are here—I take leave of my mother to seek death."
proposals.reason: 其女 refers to Huang Zhongqi's daughter Lin'annu, who then takes leave of her mother Lady Zhu.

proposals.before: Yulian hanged herself too. Three women had taken their own lives, and the bandits killed them all.
proposals.after: Yulian then hanged herself as many as three times, and the bandits killed her as well.
proposals.reason: Chinese 玉蓮因自縊者凡三，賊並殺之 records three hanging attempts by Yulian, then the rebels killing her; three women is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: In Zhizheng 19, Red Turban rebels captured Liaoyang. Zhu was then serving as Confucian Schools Intendant, and the couple took refuge from the turmoil in Zishan Temple.
proposals.after: In Zhizheng 19, Red Turban rebels captured Liaoyang. Zhu was then serving as Confucian Schools Intendant, and the couple took refuge from the turmoil in the Temple of Accumulated Good.
proposals.reason: 資善寺 means the Temple of Accumulated Good; Zishan Temple is a misleading place-name rendering.

proposals.before: Her father Defu taught in the lake and Xiang region. Tongzu was one of his students, and Defu gave him his daughter in marriage.
proposals.after: Her father Defu taught in the Hu and Xiang region. Tongzu was one of his students, and Defu gave him his daughter in marriage.
proposals.reason: The paired names Hu and Xiang denote a region, not a generic lake plus the Xiang.

proposals.before: For his military service Qi was promoted to assistant magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture, and Lady Luo was granted the title Proper Person.
proposals.after: For his military service Qi was promoted to assistant magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture, and Lady Luo was granted the title of Yiren.
proposals.reason: Yiren is the titled rank; Proper Person is an opaque calque.

proposals.before: Qi was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture for military merit; Lady Luo was enfeoffed as Yiren.
proposals.after: Qi was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture for military merit; Lady Luo was granted the title Yiren.
proposals.reason: The verb confers an honorary title rather than a territorial enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Wishing to defile her, she then with her son Rong'er and daughter Huiniang threw herself from a cliff and died.
proposals.after: Wishing to defile her, she then with her son Rong'er and daughter Huiniang threw themselves from a cliff and died.
proposals.reason: The death predicate covers mother and both children together.

proposals.before: Ne served as Censor; he died early, and Liu preserved her resolve without wavering.
proposals.after: Ne served as Investigating Censor; he died early, and Liu preserved her resolve without wavering.
proposals.reason: 監察御史 is the investigating-censor office, not the generic word Censor.

proposals.before: His daughter-in-law Lady Liu, stiffly pressing upon her mother-in-law's corpse, cursed incessantly; the soldiers killed them both.
proposals.after: His daughter-in-law Lady Liu, stiffly pressing upon her mother-in-law's corpse, cursed incessantly; the soldiers killed her as well.
proposals.reason: 並殺之 continues from the already-dead mother-in-law and records the killing of the daughter-in-law, not a simultaneous killing of both.

proposals.before: Taizhou suffered military attack; Zongyuan was then in mourning for her mother-in-law, enduring death to guard the coffin; she was seized by roving soldiers and threatened with coercion. Yuan said, "If I feared death, how could I have stayed here!
proposals.after: Taizhou suffered military attack; Zongyuan was then in mourning for her mother-in-law, risking death to guard the coffin; she was seized by roving soldiers and threatened with coercion. Yuan said, "If I feared death, how could I have stayed here!
proposals.reason: 忍死 means she risked or endured the prospect of death, not that she was 'enduring death' while still alive.

proposals.before: The couple were captured by the army. When they reached Yutian County, a man who coveted Lady Song's beauty and wished to kill Zongren—Lady Song said to her husband, "Fate has brought me to this pass. I will not let my body become your ruin."
proposals.after: The couple were captured by the army. When they reached Yutian County, there was a man who coveted Lady Song's beauty and wished to kill Zongren. Lady Song said to her husband, "Fate has brought me to this pass. I will not let my body become your ruin."
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English breaks off after the relative clause and never finishes the sentence before Lady Song speaks.

proposals.before: Xu Youtou's wife, Lady Yue, was from the capital.
proposals.after: Xu Naotou's wife, Lady Yue, was from the capital.
proposals.reason: 猱 is náo; the given English transcription Youtou does not match the Chinese nickname 猱頭.

proposals.before: Xu Youtou's wife Lady Yue was a native of the capital.
proposals.after: Xu Naotou's wife Lady Yue was a native of the capital.
proposals.reason: The literal English repeats the same unmatched transcription of 猱頭.

proposals.before: When the capital fell, she said to her daughter, "Your father has gone out to defend the city. I hold the rank of a third-grade consort, and you are both a scholar's daughter and a jinshi's wife. We cannot endure disgrace."
proposals.after: When the capital fell, she said to her daughter, "Your father has gone out to defend the city. I am a titled lady of the third rank, and you are both a Confucian family's daughter and a jinshi's wife. We cannot endure disgrace."
proposals.reason: 命婦 is the titled wife of an official, not an imperial consort; 儒家女 is specifically a Confucian family's daughter.

decisions.reason: After 生子德政, 四歲而寡 dates Dezheng's age at her widowhood, not Lady Su's; the original literal is ambiguous and readily read as her own age.
母何氏 is Lady Yao's mother; 姑 would be required for a mother-in-law, so the idiomatic in-law rendering is invented.
其母 continues 母何氏 from the preceding sentence and names Lady Yao's mother, not a mother-in-law.
負母 is the same mother; nothing in the unit supports 姑 or a mother-in-law.
In this wife-biography 舅 is paired with 姑: husband and mother-in-law guarded the stockade while 舅 remained behind ill, so he is the father-in-law, not an uncle.
舅 is the father-in-law left at home; 'father-in-law's younger brother' adds a kinship the Chinese does not state.
其舅 is the same 舅 already identified as the father-in-law who had not traveled, not a husband's uncle.
其舅 continues that father-in-law; the literal 'uncle' is the same kinship error.
愈不屈 means she became even less yielding; 'yielded all the more' inverts the negation 不屈.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 一卒以刀擊其左臂，愈不屈。

decisions.after: The bandits vied to pull her out of the water.
decisions.reason: 'Rushed in' is wrong after she had thrown herself into the river, but 出之 is extracting her from the water, not the bandits themselves rushing out; 競 marks them vying to pull her up.
許州 is Xu Prefecture; the following unit's 密邇許昌 confirms Xuchang, not 徐州 (Xuzhou).
The same 許州 is Xu Prefecture near Xuchang, not Xuzhou.
其女臨安奴 belongs to the Huang Zhongqi–Lady Zhu household just introduced; 別母 and later 朱氏母子 show she is not Zhang Shicheng's daughter.

decisions.after: In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, Zhang Shicheng attacked Hangzhou; Huang Zhongqi's daughter Lin'annu said in alarm, "The bandits are here—I take leave of my mother to seek death."
decisions.reason: 其女 is Huang Zhongqi's daughter, not Zhang Shicheng's; the proposed parenthetical 'his (Huang Zhongqi's)' is accurate in sense but awkward English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其女臨安奴倉皇言曰：「賊至矣，我別母求一死也。」

decisions.reason: 玉蓮因自縊者凡三 records three hanging attempts by Yulian, and 賊並殺之 is the bandits then killing her as well; the original invents three women, whom the Chinese does not name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 玉蓮因自縊者凡三，賊並殺之。

decisions.reason: Zishan Temple is an acceptable transcription of 資善寺; a semantic rendering is stylistic, not a correction of a factual error.
湖、湘間 is the Hu and Xiang region as a paired toponym, not a generic lake plus the Xiang River.
宜人 is the honorary rank title Yiren; 'Proper Person' is an opaque calque, not the title as used.
封宜人 confers an honorary wifely title, not a territorial enfeoffment.

decisions.after: Wishing to defile her, she together with her son Rong'er and daughter Huiniang threw themselves from a cliff and died.
decisions.reason: 投崖而死 covers mother and both children, but the proposed 'she ... threw themselves' is ungrammatical; the verb must be plural with an explicit together-with phrase.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃與子榮兒、女回娘投崖而死。

decisions.reason: 監察御史 is the office of investigating censor, not the generic word Censor.
The mother-in-law was already killed in the previous sentence (見殺); 兵並殺之 records that the soldiers then killed Lady Liu as well, not that they killed both at once.
忍死護柩 means she braved or held out against death to guard the coffin; 'enduring death' is unintelligible English while she is still alive.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宗媛方居姑喪，忍死護柩

decisions.reason: The original breaks off after the relative clause and never completes the sentence before Lady Song speaks; the repair restores a grammatical English sentence without changing the Chinese sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 有窺宋氏色美，欲害宗仁者，宋氏謂夫曰

decisions.reason: 猱 is náo; Youtou does not transcribe 猱頭.
The literal field repeats the same unmatched transcription of 猱頭; Naotou is the correct pinyin.
三品命婦 is a titled official's wife of the third rank, not an imperial consort; 儒家女 is a daughter of a Confucian family.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 我三品命婦，汝儒家女又進士妻

claimRevisions.reason: The English alias 'his daughter' was read as Zhang Shicheng's child; 其女 is Huang Zhongqi's daughter Lin'annu.
The English title calque 'Proper Person' is replaced by the rank name Yiren while the Chinese 宜人 stands.
The granted title remains 宜人; only the English label changes from the calque 'Proper Person' to Yiren.
The personal-name English was a bad transcription of 徐猱頭; Naotou matches 猱 náo.
The nickname English Youtou does not transcribe 猱頭; Naotou is the correct pinyin.
The kinship gloss inherited the unmatched transcription Youtou; the wife relation itself is unchanged.
